proposals.before: In Tianjian year four the court launched a great northern campaign; Huishao, champion chief of staff Hu Xinsheng, and pacifying-the-north general Zhang Baozi took Su prefecture, seized the city lord Ma Chenglong, and sent him to the capital.
proposals.after: In Tianjian year four the court launched a great northern campaign; Huishao, champion chief of staff Hu Xinsheng, and pacifying-the-north general Zhang Baozi took Suyu, seized the city lord Ma Chenglong, and sent him to the capital.
proposals.reason: 宿預 is the city Suyu, not a 'Su prefecture'.

proposals.before: In Tianjian year four a great northern campaign was launched; Huishao with champion chief of staff Hu Xinsheng and pacifying-the-north general Zhang Baozi attacked Su prefecture, seized city lord Ma Chenglong, and sent him to the capital.
proposals.after: In Tianjian year four a great northern campaign was launched; Huishao with champion chief of staff Hu Xinsheng and pacifying-the-north general Zhang Baozi attacked Suyu, seized city lord Ma Chenglong, and sent him to the capital.
proposals.reason: 宿預 is Suyu; the literal field repeats the same mistranslation.

proposals.before: Soon Wei reinforcements came in force, defeated Huangong and took him; Huishao could not hold the line and fled to Huaiyin that night, and Wei retook Su prefecture.
proposals.after: Soon Wei reinforcements came in force, defeated Huangong and took him; Huishao could not hold the line and fled to Huaiyin that night, and Wei retook Suyu.
proposals.reason: 宿預 should be Suyu throughout, not Su prefecture.

proposals.before: Before long Wei reinforcements arrived in great numbers, defeated and captured Huangong; Huishao could not hold, that night fled back to Huaiyin, and Wei again took Su prefecture.
proposals.after: Before long Wei reinforcements arrived in great numbers, defeated and captured Huangong; Huishao could not hold, that night fled back to Huaiyin, and Wei again took Suyu.
proposals.reason: 宿預 is Suyu, not Su prefecture.

proposals.before: When Wei's garrisons at Su prefecture and Huaiyang came over, Huishao won them over with merit, was raised to wise martial general, and gained two hundred more households.
proposals.after: When Wei's garrisons at Suyu and Huaiyang came over, Huishao won them over with merit, was raised to wise martial general, and gained two hundred more households.
proposals.reason: 宿預 is Suyu, not Su prefecture.

proposals.before: When Wei's Su prefecture and Huaiyang cities surrendered inward, Huishao comforted and received them with merit, was advanced to wise martial general, and his fief increased by two hundred households.
proposals.after: When Wei's Suyu and Huaiyang cities surrendered inward, Huishao comforted and received them with merit, was advanced to wise martial general, and his fief increased by two hundred households.
proposals.reason: 宿預 is Suyu, not Su prefecture.

proposals.before: Late in Qi Jianwu, Wei's Tuoba Hong overran Nan Yang and five commanderies; Mingdi sent Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to win them back.
proposals.after: Late in Qi Jianwu, Wei's Tuoba Hong overran the five commanderies including Nanyang; Mingdi sent Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to win them back.
proposals.reason: 南陽等五郡 means five commanderies including Nanyang, not Nanyang plus five more.

proposals.before: Late in Qi Jianwu, Wei ruler Tuoba Hong raided and captured Nan Yang and five other commanderies; Mingdi sent Grand Marshal Chen Xianda with a host to recover them.
proposals.after: Late in Qi Jianwu, Wei ruler Tuoba Hong raided and captured the five commanderies including Nanyang; Mingdi sent Grand Marshal Chen Xianda with a host to recover them.
proposals.reason: 等五郡 is five in total including Nanyang, not five other commanderies.

proposals.before: Daogen said: "Timidity guards against courage in battle—that is the saying."
proposals.after: Daogen said: "Guard timidly, fight bravely—that is the saying."
proposals.reason: 怯防勇戰 means timid defense paired with brave fighting, not timidity guarding against courage.

proposals.before: His fief grew by three hundred households and he was raised to marquis.
proposals.after: His fief grew by three hundred households and he was raised to earl.
proposals.reason: 進爵爲伯 advances the rank to bo (earl/count), not marquis (hou); he had been 縣男.

proposals.before: His fief increased by three hundred households and he was advanced to marquis.
proposals.after: His fief increased by three hundred households and he was advanced to earl.
proposals.reason: Chinese 伯 is earl/count, not marquis.

proposals.before: Gaozu once pointed at Daogen to show Director of the Court for Public Works Shen Yue: "This man's mouth does not discuss merit."
proposals.after: Gaozu once pointed at Daogen to show Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue: "This man's mouth does not discuss merit."
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is the Director of the Imperial Secretariat / Department of State Affairs, not the Court for Public Works.

proposals.before: In Song's early Yongchu years Mu led three thousand-odd township families south of Xiangyang's Xian.
proposals.after: In Song's early Yongchu years Mu led more than three thousand township families into the south of Mount Xian at Xiangyang.
proposals.reason: 峴南 is the south of Mount Xian, not a toponym Xian possessed by Xiangyang.

proposals.before: In the early Yongchu era of Song, Mu led more than three thousand families of the township into the south of Xiangyang's Xian.
proposals.after: In the early Yongchu era of Song, Mu led more than three thousand families of the township into the south of Mount Xian at Xiangyang.
proposals.reason: Literal 襄陽之峴南 names Mount Xian south of Xiangyang.

proposals.before: When Qi Wendi governed Yongzhou he took only men of great families; Xuan alone entered as Western Bureau secretary on merit.
proposals.after: When Qi Wendi governed Yongzhou he took only men of great families; Xuan was specially summoned for his ability as Western Bureau Secretary.
proposals.reason: 特以才力 means specially for his ability, not that he alone was appointed.

proposals.before: When Qi Wendi was Yongzhou Inspector his recruits were all drawn from great houses; Xuan alone was summoned for talent as Western Bureau Secretary.
proposals.after: When Qi Wendi was Yongzhou Inspector his recruits were all drawn from great houses; Xuan was specially summoned for talent as Western Bureau Secretary.
proposals.reason: 特 does not mean alone.

proposals.before: When Mount Xiong's outlaws handed their walls to Wei, Xuan sent Major Huo Fengbo ahead to seize the heights.
proposals.after: When Mount Qu's outlaws handed their walls to Wei, Xuan sent Major Huo Fengbo ahead to seize the heights.
proposals.reason: 朐山 is Mount Qu (Ju), not Xiong (胸).

proposals.before: When fugitives at Mount Xiong surrendered the city to Wei, Xuan galloped and sent his Major Huo Fengbo to divide the army and hold the passes.
proposals.after: When fugitives at Mount Qu surrendered the city to Wei, Xuan galloped and sent his Major Huo Fengbo to divide the army and hold the passes.
proposals.reason: 朐山 is Mount Qu, not Xiong.

proposals.before: Wei came and could not pass Xiong city.
proposals.after: Wei came and could not pass Qu city.
proposals.reason: 朐城 is Qu city, matching 朐山, not Xiong.

proposals.before: The Wei army came but could not cross beyond Xiong city.
proposals.after: The Wei army came but could not cross beyond Qu city.
proposals.reason: 朐城 is Qu city, not Xiong.

proposals.before: He entered service as the Prince of Linchuan's chief of staff and left valiant cavalry general, then became vermilion-robe attendant.
proposals.after: He was summoned as Chief of Staff to the General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Linchuan, given the added rank Left Valiant Cavalry General, then soon transferred to Vermilion-Robe Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 驃騎 is General of Agile Cavalry attached to the Prince of Linchuan, not omitted.

proposals.before: He was summoned as Chief of Staff to the Prince of Linchuan, Pacifies-the-Frontier Cavalry General, and soon transferred to Vermilion-Robe Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: He was summoned as Chief of Staff to the General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Linchuan, given the added rank Left Valiant Cavalry General, and soon transferred to Vermilion-Robe Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 驃騎 is not Pacifies-the-Frontier; 加左驍騎將軍 is omitted from the literal English.

proposals.before: In year thirteen he became crown prince right guard leader with a hundred armored men, on palace duty with Xiao Jingzhi.
proposals.after: In year thirteen he became Crown Prince Right Guard Leader with a hundred armored men, on palace duty with Xiao Jing.
proposals.reason: The name is 蕭景, not Xiao Jingzhi.

proposals.before: In the thirteenth year he was made Crown Prince Right Guard Leader with a hundred men in armor, dwelling in the palace with Area Commander Xiao Jingzhi.
proposals.after: In the thirteenth year he was made Crown Prince Right Guard Leader with a hundred men in armor, dwelling in the palace with Army Leader Xiao Jing.
proposals.reason: 領軍 is Leader of the Army, not Area Commander; 蕭景 is Xiao Jing.

proposals.before: That day he had artists paint Xuan and sent an emissary with the scroll: "Do you know this face?"
proposals.after: That day he had artists paint Xuan and sent an emissary with the scroll: "Do you know this picture?"
proposals.reason: 圖 is a picture, not a face; the Chinese asks 卿識此圖不.

proposals.before: Gaozu agreed and sent Chen Chengbai and Zu Chong to survey; all said the Huai's sand was loose and shifting and the work would never hold.
proposals.after: Gaozu agreed and sent Chen Chengbai and Zu Geng to survey; all said the Huai's sand was loose and shifting and the work would never hold.
proposals.reason: 祖暅 is Zu Geng, not Zu Chong.

proposals.before: Gaozu overruled them and drafted Xu and Yang, one man from every five households in a group of twenty.
proposals.after: Gaozu overruled them and drafted the people of Xu and Yang, taking five adult males from every twenty households.
proposals.reason: 率二十戶取五丁 means five ding from twenty households, not one man from every five households.

proposals.before: Gaozu would not accept it and mobilized men of Xu and Yang, taking one man from every five households of twenty.
proposals.after: Gaozu would not accept it and mobilized men of Xu and Yang, taking five adult males from every twenty households.
proposals.reason: 二十戶取五丁 is five laborers per twenty households.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month Li Xianding of Wei led the armies; Xuan and Liu Sigu of Xuzhou met them.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Li Tanding of Wei led the armies; Xuan and Liu Sizu of Xuzhou met them.
proposals.reason: 劉思祖 is Liu Sizu; 李曇定 is Li Tanding, not Xianding.

proposals.before: The water ran clear; looking down you could see the graves of the living below as if on a map.
proposals.after: The water ran clear; looking down you could see the inhabitants' graves below, every one distinct.
proposals.reason: 居人墳墓 are the graves of the people who dwelt there, not graves of the living.

proposals.before: After Xuan left, Baozi let the dam rot; in autumn of the eighth month the Huai burst and the whole work collapsed into the sea, and Zu Chong went to prison.
proposals.after: After Xuan left, Baozi let the dam rot; in autumn of the eighth month the Huai burst and the whole work collapsed into the sea, and Zu Geng went to prison.
proposals.reason: 祖暅 is Zu Geng; English Chong does not match the given name 暅.

proposals.before: After Xuan left, Baozi did not maintain the dam; by autumn in the eighth month the Huai swelled violently and the dam broke entirely, rushing to the sea, and Zu Chong was imprisoned.
proposals.after: After Xuan left, Baozi did not maintain the dam; by autumn in the eighth month the Huai swelled violently and the dam broke entirely, rushing to the sea, and Zu Geng was imprisoned.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise renders 祖暅 as Zu Chong rather than Zu Geng.

proposals.before: Xuan was mild and slow to fear; in court he looked as though he could not find words, and men called him long-suffering.
proposals.after: Xuan was mild and seldom showed joy or fear; in court he looked as though he could not find words, and men called him generous and honest.
proposals.reason: 少喜懼 means seldom showing joy or fear; 長厚 means generous and honest, not long-suffering.

proposals.before: Xuan was easy and seldom fearful; at court he seemed before others as if he could not speak, and was called long in forbearance.
proposals.after: Xuan was easygoing and seldom showed joy or fear; at court he seemed before others as if he could not speak, and was called generous and honest.
proposals.reason: 長厚 is generous and honest character, not forbearance; 少喜懼 includes both joy and fear.

proposals.before: For merit he gained Army Adviser General, two hundred more households, and moved to bearer of credentials, area commander of Qing and Ji, expeditionary general, and inspector of both provinces.
proposals.after: For merit he was advanced to Army Adviser General, his fief increased by two hundred households, and he was transferred to Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of Qing and Ji military affairs, General Who Campaigns Against the Caitiffs, and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
proposals.reason: 征虜將軍 is the titled generalship Campaigns-Against-the-Caitiffs, not a generic expeditionary general.

proposals.before: For merit he was advanced to Army Adviser General, his fief increased by two hundred households, and he was transferred to Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of all Qing and Ji military affairs, Expeditionary General, and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
proposals.after: For merit he was advanced to Army Adviser General, his fief increased by two hundred households, and he was transferred to Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of all Qing and Ji military affairs, General Who Campaigns Against the Caitiffs, and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 征虜將軍 as Expeditionary General, which drops the 虜 element of the office name.

proposals.before: Posthumously he shall be made regular attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and chariot-and-cavalry general, with pipes and drums as well.
proposals.after: Posthumously he shall be made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chariot and Cavalry General, with pipes and drums as well.
proposals.reason: 散騎常侍 is one office; the idiomatic line duplicates attendant language into an unreadable double title.

proposals.before: He may be posthumously made Regular Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry, with one set of martial pipes and drums as well.
proposals.after: He may be posthumously made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry, with one set of martial pipes and drums as well.
proposals.reason: The literal line likewise stacks Regular Attendant onto Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for a single 散騎常侍.

decisions.reason: 宿預 is the place Suyu, not a prefecture named Su; 攻宿預 names that city, and 城主 confirms a city command rather than a 州.
The literal field repeats the same error: 宿預 is Suyu, not Su prefecture.
魏復得宿預 repeats the same toponym; Wei recaptured Suyu, not a Su prefecture.
The literal likewise misreads 宿預 as Su prefecture; Suyu is the correct place-name.
魏宿預、淮陽二城 names two cities; 宿預 is Suyu, paired with Huaiyang, not Su prefecture.
The literal again renders 宿預 as Su prefecture; the two cities are Suyu and Huaiyang.
南陽等五郡 is five commanderies in all, including Nanyang, not Nanyang plus five more.
The literal's 'Nan Yang and five other commanderies' inflates 等五郡 to six; the total is five including Nanyang.
怯防勇戰 is a paired formula, timid defense and brave fighting, not 'timidity guarding against courage.' The proposed saying matches the Chinese and the already-correct idiomatic line.
進爵爲伯 advances the noble rank to 伯 (earl/count). Marquis would be 侯; the original 'marquis' is the wrong rank.
The literal likewise translates 伯 as marquis; earl is the correct rank term here.
尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat (Department of State Affairs). Court for Public Works is a different office and is not in the Chinese.
襄陽之峴南 is the south of Mount Xian in the Xiangyang area, not a place 'Xian' possessed by Xiangyang.
The literal should likewise name Mount Xian; 峴南 is not 'Xiangyang's Xian.'
特以才力 marks a special summons for ability against a background of famous-family appointments; 特 does not mean that Xuan was the only recruit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 絢特以才力召爲西曹書佐

decisions.reason: The literal's 'alone' is the same misreading of 特; 'specially summoned for talent' is what the Chinese says.
朐山 is Mount Qu (朐), not Xiong (胸). The original English misreads the character.
The literal repeats Mount Xiong for 朐山; Mount Qu is the correct name.
朐城 is the city at 朐, matching 朐山 in the previous sentence, not Xiong city.
The literal likewise misreads 朐城 as Xiong city; Qu city follows 朐.
徵驃騎臨川王司馬 makes Xuan Sima to the Agile-Cavalry Prince of Linchuan; 驃騎 is omitted in the original, and 加左驍騎將軍 is an added rank before 尋轉朱衣直閤.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徵驃騎臨川王司馬，加左驍騎將軍，尋轉朱衣直閤

decisions.reason: 驃騎 is not Pacifies-the-Frontier, and the literal drops 加左驍騎將軍. The replacement restores both the prince's cavalry title and the added Left Valiant Cavalry General.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徵驃騎臨川王司馬，加左驍騎將軍

decisions.reason: 與領軍蕭景直殿內 names 蕭景 (Xiao Jing) on palace duty; 直殿內 is the duty phrase, not part of the personal name Xiao Jingzhi.
領軍 is Leader of the Army, not Area Commander, and the person is 蕭景, not Xiao Jingzhi.
The emperor asks 卿識此圖不, pointing to the painted 圖, not to a 'face.'
祖暅 is Zu Geng; 暅 is Geng, not Chong.
率二十戶取五丁 levies five adult males from every twenty households, not one man from every five households.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 率二十戶取五丁以築之

decisions.reason: The literal's 'one man from every five households of twenty' garbles 二十戶取五丁; five ding per twenty households is the levy.
李曇定 is Li Tanding (曇, not 顯) and 劉思祖 is Liu Sizu, not Liu Sigu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李曇定督衆軍來戰，絢與徐州刺史劉思祖等距之

decisions.reason: 居人墳墓 are the graves of the people who had lived there. 'Graves of the living' is a mistranslation, and 'as if on a map' invents 了然, which means the graves were plainly visible.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 俯視居人墳墓，了然皆在其下

decisions.reason: 祖暅 is again Zu Geng; imprisoning 'Zu Chong' after the dam burst misnames the same 暅.
The literal repeats Zu Chong for 祖暅; Zu Geng is the correct English name.
少喜懼 means he seldom showed joy or fear, not merely that he was slow to fear. 長厚 is generous and honest character, not 'long-suffering.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 絢寬和少喜懼……號爲長厚

decisions.reason: The literal omits 喜 from 少喜懼 and renders 長厚 as forbearance; generous and honest matches 長厚, and both joy and fear belong in 喜懼.
征虜將軍 is the named generalship 'who campaigns against the caitiffs,' not a generic expeditionary general; the rest of the proposed titles follows 持節、督青冀二州諸軍事 and 青冀二州刺史.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 征虜將軍、青冀二州刺史

decisions.reason: The literal's Expeditionary General drops 虜 from 征虜將軍; General Who Campaigns Against the Caitiffs is the office named in the Chinese.
散騎常侍 is a single office, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary. Stacking 'regular attendant' onto that title invents a second post.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 可贈散騎常侍、車騎將軍

decisions.reason: The literal likewise doubles Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for one 散騎常侍.

claimRevisions.reason: The name fact remains, but 蕭景 is Xiao Jing; Jingzhi was created by attaching 直殿內 to the name.
The person 祖暅 remains; English Chong does not render 暅, which is Geng.
The name fact remains, but 曇 is Tan, not Xian; the English must be Li Tanding to match 李曇定.
The name fact remains; 思祖 is Sizu, not Sigu.
The person 祖暅 remains; English Chong and pinyin Xuan both fail to render 暅 (Geng).
The given-name fact remains 暅, but its English value Chong is unsupported; Geng is the reading.
